why: Best overall score (TOPSIS) for your priorities 'this_farmer': profit 30%, water saving 30%, salt tolerance 20%.
Sequence: wheat → fallow → wheat → fallow → barley → fallow. Every crop keeps ≥ 100% of its potential yield at your well's 10 dS/m when the leaching water is applied.
evidence: NASA POWER 1981–2025 (CERES radiation; MERRA-2 temperature, humidity, wind, rain) at the DRC Ras Sudr pixel: FAO-56 reference ET 1,912 mm/yr vs only 47 mm/yr of rain.
Summer days above 35 °C: 28 per year on average (POWER T2M_MAX); MERRA-2 root-zone wetness (GWETROOT) in summer ≈ 0.29 — the soil is dry without irrigation.

Stress test on 5,400 simulated 3-year futures (45 years of NASA climate, +1/+2 °C, −10/−20% rain, saltier well and CMIP6 2050s futures, and 100/70/40 % of the leaching water): this plan held up in 0% of them.
Landsat 1990–2025: green area (yearly NDVI P90 > 0.25, land only; matches S16 within 25 %) in the Ras Sudr plain grew from 51 ha (1996) to 1,208 ha (2022).
Sentinel-2 finds 122 cultivated fields (125 ha) nearby; the most common pattern over the last 3 years is perennial/perennial (winter/summer).
SMAP root-zone moisture: 0.08 m³/m³ in summer vs 0.08 in winter.
GPM IMERG 2001–2025: 28 mm/yr, 0.4 days/yr above 10 mm.
MODIS land-surface temperature in June–August averages 37 °C.
NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (5 models, 2041–2060): Tmax +1.6 °C (SSP2-4.5) to +2.1 °C (SSP5-8.5) — included in the stress test.
GRACE/GRACE-FO regional water storage trend: -0.68 cm/yr (coarse, regional).
Yields calibrated on the DRC Ras Sudr barley trial (S1: 4,215 kg/ha at ECw 8.35); soil salinity on S4 (ECe 8.56 at ECw 7.94).
benefits: Net profit 89,390 EGP in 3 years (+19% vs your current 75,008 EGP); ≈ 5,959 EGP per feddan per year.

Saves 7% water (9,430 vs 10,173 m³ in 3 years).
Builds soil nitrogen (legumes): 25 vs 24 mg/kg.
gaps: Prices/costs are estimates (no 2025-26 Egyptian quote found) for: barley — see data/prices_egp.csv.

This pick is sensitive: a ±20 % change in `opt.min_cropped_slots`, `ws.ea_drip`, `ymax.squash` can change it (sensitivity analysis).
The plan uses the station's climate and soil; your own field's NDVI history is on the map — pick your field to compare.
risks: Measure THIS well's salinity (ECw) every season — Ras Sudr wells range from 3 to 38 dS/m and the 'highly saline' share of the aquifer rose from 52% (1996) to 83% (2022).
Wheat (bread) (W1, W2) needs 50% extra water for leaching; without it the yield could fall to about 36% (FAO-29 at LF 15%).
Barley (W3) needs 33% extra water for leaching; without it the yield could fall to about 65% (FAO-29 at LF 15%).
If you apply only 70 % / 40 % of the leaching water the plan passes 0% / 0% of futures (salt builds up in 100% / 100%). The S1 trial applied about 60 % of the FAO-29 amount.
Weakest case: Past climate 1981–2025 — passes 0% of the time; main cause: salt builds up in the soil.
Decision support only — confirm with your local agricultural extension officer.
